page: Microsoft Azure DS11_v2 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the DSv2 family, built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, with 2 physical cores and a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 14.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 29 GB of local storage and does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the DS11_v2 delivers modest compute capabilities. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests falls into the bottom 25%, while Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores rank in the bottom 10%. Memory performance is a relative highlight, with the Passmark memory score reaching the middle 50% tier, though uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth remains in the bottom 25% at 23.32 GB/sec and 18.23 GB/sec respectively. Cryptographic and compression tasks show weak to poor performance, with Passmark CPU encryption in the bottom 10% and single-threaded gzip compression in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the DS11_v2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.0 GB per core, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense CPU processing. However, the tradeoff is its weak overall compute performance, as evidenced by poor scores in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. It is best suited for lightweight database operations, basic web serving, or small-scale text and image processing tasks where memory capacity is prioritized over raw processing speed.
